doc.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Joining and playing with Miles Davis
title: Dave Holland joins Miles, DeJohnette follows, and the Directions session
summary: Miles hires Holland, DeJohnette encourages him to stay, Tony leaves and DeJohnette joins Miles for his first session.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: I don’t think Mikell’s was even open then.

No… you’d know the name. Dave goes and plays with Miles. Tony’s controlling the band and it just so happened that Ron Carter was in the house and Miles asked Ron to come up and play, and Ron played some…
So Ron had already left the band?

For Dave it was like… Dave felt under some pressure there and I convinced him, “Come on man! Stick it out!” because he was ready to go back to England and I said, “Oh man you don’t want to do that, this is an opportunity, man. Stay here!” Of course the rest is history.
So had Ron already left the band?
Yeah Ron had left… Herbie was playing. Then Chick was there. Herbie was leaving and Tony was leaving so one by one each one left. Then when Tony left, they called me to join the band.
Well the discography reflects that you recorded that one session in I believe September of 68’, played “Directions.” Do you remember that session?
That was your first session with Miles.
Yeah “Directions.” I think that had a couple of keyboard players on it. Two or three keyboard players and Wayne and Dave. Maybe it wasn’t. I think it was just the quintet if I’m not mistaken.
